Article Title: 'Propaganda against E20 was a paid campaign': Nitin Gadkari as govt paves way for E100 fuel
Article Text:
Nitin Gadkari says E20 criticism has faded, backs ethanol push to cut oil imports

What was E20 controversy about

NEW DELHI: Union road transport minister Nitin Gadkari on Tuesday described the backlash against petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) as a “paid campaign”. His remarks came a day after the government notified changes to motor vehicle rules allowing flex-fuel vehicles to run on blends containing up to 100% ethanol.Speaking at an event organised by industry body CII, Gadkari said the opposition to E20 had intensified about three months ago but had since subsided.“Three months ago, huge noise (khub halla) was made against the E20 (20 per cent ethanol-blended petrol) fuel; now rage against E20 fuel is over...It was a paid campaign,” news agency PTI quoted Gadkari as saying.The government on Monday notified amendments to the Central Motor Vehicles Rules, 1989, permitting flex-fuel vehicles capable of running on fuel containing up to E100, or nearly pure ethanol.Gadkari has repeatedly advocated greater use of ethanol as part of efforts to reduce the country's dependence on imported fossil fuels. He said expanding the use of alternative fuels could help the country save valuable foreign exchange by cutting fossil fuel imports.The Centre’s nationwide rollout of petrol blended with 20% ethanol (E20) had triggered protests and political criticism earlier this year, with motorists raising concerns over reduced mileage and the compatibility of the fuel with older vehicles.Opposition leaders questioned the government’s decision to make E20 the standard fuel at petrol pumps across India in April 2025.The row escalated after attorney general R Venkataramani referred to E20 as an “experiment” during a Supreme Court hearing, saying its results would be known next year. The remark went viral, prompting renewed criticism of the policy.The Centre subsequently clarified that the attorney general was referring to ethanol supply volumes, not describing the E20 policy itself as an experiment. Venkataramani also told Reuters that his comments had been misunderstood.The government and automobile industry cited studies indicating that E20 does not significantly damage metallic engine components, while acknowledging that fuel efficiency and compatibility can vary across vehicles.
Article Summary: Road transport minister Nitin Gadkari says E20 criticism has faded, backs ethanol push to cut oil imports. His remarks came a day after the government notified changes to motor vehicle rules allowing flex-fuel vehicles to run on blends containing up to 100% ethanol.

Article Title: 'Apologise to nation': Rijiju targets Congress after Army debunks Chinese intrusion claims
Article Text:
Army debunks fake AI video on China, Rijiju demands Congress apology

NEW DELHI: Bhartiya Janata Party on Tuesday hit out at the Congress for circulating an AI-generated video falsely attributing claims about Chinese control of areas in Arunachal Pradesh to an Indian Army officer, escalating the political face-off over the clip.Leading the BJP's counterattack, Union minister Kiren Rijiju accused the Congress of sharing the fabricated video featuring Lieutenant General Girish Kalia and demanded an apology for allegedly tarnishing the Army's image.In a post on X, Rijiju demanded an apology from the opposition party, writing, "Congress Party must apologize to the nation for spreading fake AI video to tarnish the image of Indian Army.""This is a treacherous act and is on par with the vile deeds of our enemies. The Congress Party is running a despicable campaign on behalf of India's enemies," the Union minister added.The row erupted after Congress shared a post on Monday alleging that China had captured the three areas in Arunachal Pradesh.Congress leader Ritu Choudhary on X wrote: "Shameful! Lieutenant General Girish Kalia (GOC, Spear Corps) says that China has captured Asafila, Longju, and Taksing circles in Arunachal Pradesh.Despite demands for logistics (supplies), there are reports that the army is being deployed against 'Gen Z' instead of China," Choudhary wrote.The Indian Army's fact-check unit also debunked the viral video, saying it had been digitally altered and contained fabricated remarks attributed to the officer.In a post on X, the Army said: "A digitally altered video is being circulated with fabricated remarks attributed to Lt Gen Girish Kalia, claiming that China has taken control of Asaphila, Longjou and Taksing Circle in Arunachal Pradesh and that the Indian Army has been denied essential supplies. The misleading video attempts to portray fabricated statements as a leaked admission by a senior Indian Army officer. The video uses Synthetic Generated Information to falsely attribute remarks to Lt Gen Girish Kalia. The original footage relates to a press briefing delivered by then GOC 28 Infantry Division, Maj Gen Girish Kalia, in Kupwara, Jammu & Kashmir, on 27 October 2023. He addressed infiltration attempts across the Line of Control, reporting 10 foiled attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of warlike stores and narcotics.He made no such statements about Chinese control over Arunachal Pradesh or denial of supplies to the Indian Army..."The Army clarified that the original footage was from a press briefing held in Kupwara, Jammu and Kashmir, on October 27, 2023, when then Major General Girish Kalia spoke about infiltration attempts across the Line of Control. According to the Army, he reported 10 foiled infiltration attempts, the elimination of 27 terrorists and the recovery of weapons and narcotics.The Army said the officer had made no statements about Chinese control over areas in Arunachal Pradesh or the denial of supplies to Indian troops.
Article Summary: Bhartiya Janata Party hits out at Congress for circulating fake AI video on China. Union minister Kiren Rijiju demands an apology for tarnishing the Army's image. Indian Army's fact-check unit also debunked the viral video, saying it had been digitally altered.

Article Title: SIR row: Supreme Court defers hearing, grants petitioner 10 days to reply to EC's counter-affidavit
Article Text:
SC granted petitioner 10 days to respond to the EC’s defence of its functioning and the SIR exercise, deferring the hearing until after Diwali

What the EC told SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has deferred hearing on a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of the Election Commission (EC), including allegations that Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar took unilateral decisions on matters that required unanimous approval, particularly in connection with the special intensive revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.A bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant granted petitioner Rakesh Kumar Singh 10 days to file a rejoinder to the EC’s counter-affidavit, which was submitted on Monday night. Senior advocate Vikas Singh, appearing for the petitioner, sought time to respond to the poll body's submissions.The matter is likely to be listed on November 17, after the Diwali vacation and completion of the 10-day period.The petitions challenge the ECI’s decision-making process and seek to invalidate the SIR exercise and related actions. Singh’s plea also sought the suspension of the CEC over allegations of unilateral decision-making.In its counter-affidavit, the ECI defended its functioning and the conduct of the SIR exercise, rejecting allegations of irregularities and questioning the basis of the petition.The affidavit was unanimously approved by Kumar and Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi. The ECI said all three SIR orders issued in June 2025, October 2025 and May 2026 were unanimous decisions of the Commission.The poll body also maintained that notes, queries or suggestions made by individual commissioners while files are being processed do not constitute decisions of the Commission. It said files are routed through one Election Commissioner, then the other, and finally the CEC, while urgent approvals may be obtained electronically and recorded on file later.On allegations concerning changes to voter enrolment forms, the ECI said Form 6 had not been amended and that only the Centre could make such changes. However, it acknowledged that the online display could be interpreted as an amendment and said that, from October 21, the online application would be split into Form 6 and a separate SIR declaration, in line with the physical form.The Commission also said voters whose records could not be mapped during the SIR need not attend hearings as a rule, with booth-level officers (BLOs) collecting documents from their homes.Hearings would be held only in exceptional cases, preferably online.On the ECINet electoral database, the poll body said no name could be added or deleted without an order from the Electoral Registration Officer (ERO). It added that a committee involving experts from IIT and IISc had been set up to examine compliance.The ECI further argued that a plea seeking to restrain the CEC was not maintainable, stating that the CEC could be removed only through the process applicable to a Supreme Court judge.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has deferred hearing on a batch of petitions challenging the functioning of the Election Commission. The petitions challenge the ECI’s decision-making process and seek to invalidate the SIR exercise and related actions. The matter is likely to be listed on November 17, after the Diwali vacation.

Article Title: Who named Cyclone Arnab and why? Where it will hit, states on alert and preparedness
Article Text:
Rough sea conditions prevail ahead of the expected landfall, in Visakhapatnam, Andhra Pradesh

Why is it named Arnab? How storm naming works

Andhra Pradesh braces for landfall

Odisha, Jharkhand face heavy rain, strong winds

West Bengal, Uttar Pradesh also likely to see unseasonal rain

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

India is bracing for Cyclone Arnab as it moves towards the Andhra Pradesh coast, with landfall expected by Wednesday forenoon as authorities expect strong winds, heavy rainfall and possible flooding across several states.Cyclone Arnab is drawing attention not only for its projected impact along the Andhra Pradesh coast but also for its name.Meanwhile, the India Meteorological Department (IMD) has forecast maximum sustained wind speeds of 115-125 kmph, with gusts reaching 140 kmph, when the storm crosses the coast near Yanam, between Bapatla and Visakhapatnam. Its effects are expected in Andhra Pradesh, Odisha, Jharkhand, West Bengal and Uttar Pradesh, prompting weather alerts and precautionary measures.The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. It is pronounced “Ornab”.Cyclone names in the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea are assigned by the World Meteorological Organization (WMO)/United Nations Economic and Social Commission for Asia and the Pacific (ESCAP) Panel on Tropical Cyclones. The naming system began in 2004, with the list subsequently expanded as more countries joined the panel.The current list contains 52 names contributed by 13 countries: Bangladesh, India, Iran, Maldives, Myanmar, Oman, Pakistan, Qatar, Saudi Arabia, Sri Lanka, Thailand, the United Arab Emirates and Yemen. The list was adopted in April 2020.Names are used sequentially, column-wise, according to the established list. Each name is used only once and is not repeated in subsequent lists. The Regional Specialised Meteorological Centre in New Delhi, operated by the IMD, is responsible for naming cyclones that form over the Bay of Bengal and Arabian Sea once they reach the prescribed intensity.Naming storms helps meteorological agencies, governments, disaster management authorities and the public identify and communicate warnings about individual weather systems more easily.The cyclone was centred over the west-central Bay of Bengal on Tuesday morning, moving west-northwestwards before its expected turn towards the coast. The Andhra Pradesh State Disaster Management Authority (APSDMA) has warned of heavy rainfall in northern coastal districts, including Srikakulam, with strong winds already affecting parts of the coast.Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas, as potentially vulnerable. According to the state disaster management authorities, 1,763 cyclone shelters have been readied, 2,907 control rooms established and 3,185 nodal officers deployed. National and state disaster response teams have also been positioned in 11 high-risk districts.Authorities have banned public access to beaches and announced restrictions on coastal road movement. Fishing vessels have been secured at harbours, with the APSDMA saying 30,043 fishing vessels have been anchored.Air India has warned that adverse weather could affect flights to and from Visakhapatnam and Vijayawada on October 27. Passengers have been advised to check their flight status and allow additional time for travel to airports.Ashwini Vaishnaw said safety protocols and rapid restoration measures were in place across the Vijayawada and Visakhapatnam divisions ahead of Cyclone Arnab’s expected landfall on October 28. In a post on X, he said war rooms were active at zonal, divisional and Railway Board levels, with around 600 km of track under close watch. “Passenger safety is the top priority,” Vaishnaw said, adding that relief wagons, diesel locomotives, ambulances and restoration equipment had been stationed at key locations, while wind speeds and water levels were being monitored hourly. He also said coordination with the National Disaster Response Force (NDRF) and state disaster authorities was under way.Odisha has already experienced heavy rain and strong winds in parts of the state. The IMD has issued an orange warning for heavy to very heavy rainfall, ranging from 12 cm to 20 cm, in Puri, Gajapati, Ganjam, Rayagada, Koraput and Malkangiri. A yellow warning has been issued for several other districts.Tourist boat and ferry operations at Chilika Lake have been suspended from October 26 to 29 as a precaution. Authorities have moved boats to safer locations, while Paradip Port has provided shelter to 305 fishermen at its Eastern Quay-1 berth.In Jharkhand, the state government has directed district administrations to remain vigilant. A yellow alert for heavy rain has been issued for several districts on October 28, followed by orange alerts for parts of the state through October 30. Thunderstorms, lightning and gusty winds are also expected.The Ranchi district administration has warned of waterlogging, overflowing drains and water bodies, damage to weak structures and possible flood-like conditions in low-lying areas. Standing crops could also be affected by water accumulation.The cyclone's influence is expected to extend to West Bengal between October 28 and 30. In south Bengal, heavy rainfall is forecast in South 24 Parganas, Purba Medinipur, Paschim Medinipur, Jhargram, Purulia, Bankura and Paschim Bardhaman on October 28 and 29. Kolkata is likely to receive light to moderate rain over the next 48 hours.In the sub-Himalayan region, Darjeeling, Kalimpong, Alipurduar and Jalpaiguri are likely to experience heavy rain on October 29 and 30. The IMD has also advised fishermen not to venture into the sea until October 29, warning of rough to very rough conditions and squally winds of 40-50 kmph, gusting up to 60 kmph, along and off the West Bengal coast.Uttar Pradesh is forecast to receive unseasonal rain, thunderstorms and strong winds between October 28 and 31. The IMD has issued alerts for several districts, with heavy rain possible in parts of eastern Uttar Pradesh, Awadh and the Terai region. Daytime temperatures could fall by 5-8 degrees Celsius in some areas on October 30.Authorities have advised residents to follow official weather bulletins, avoid unnecessary travel during storms and stay away from trees, electricity poles, weak structures and open fields during lightning.
Article Summary: Cyclone Arnab is drawing attention not only for its projected impact along the Andhra Pradesh coast but also for its name. The name Arnab was contributed by Bangladesh to the list of names used for tropical cyclones over the North Indian Ocean. Authorities have identified 16 districts, covering 2,460 revenue villages and 92 urban areas as potentially vulnerable.

Article Title: SC seeks Centre’s response to media body’s plea challenging data protection act
Article Text:
SC asks for Centre's reply against Data Protection Act

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

RTI amendment also challenged

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Tuesday issued notice to the Centre on a petition filed by the Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) challenging provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and its accompanying rules. The association had alleged that the act infringe press freedom and the right to information.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana issued the notice after hearing senior advocate Madhavi Divan, appearing for the DNPA. The matter will be heard next on November 17 along with pending petitions.The plea seeks to strike down several provisions of the law, arguing that the absence of an exemption for journalistic activities could impede reporting, undermine investigative journalism and compromise the confidentiality of sources.Describing the petition as a comprehensive challenge by traditional news organisations, Divan told the bench, “This is perhaps the first comprehensive petition by what we call legacy media. There has been some debate over citizen journalists. We are the traditional, conventional legacy media.”She sought an interim stay on the challenged provisions, arguing that consent requirements could make routine and time-sensitive reporting difficult.“If I am left to the mercy of the data principal as to whether he or she will give consent, how will news be reported?” she asked.Divan also warned that the provisions could affect live television coverage and restrict newsrooms from reporting without prior permission.“What is the point if I have to ask for permission and consent,” she asked.According to Reuters, media groups told the court that the law amounted to pre-censorship and could force newsrooms to shut down. The challenge involves 21 news publishers.The DNPA has also challenged the amendment to Section 8(1)(j) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, arguing that it restricts access to information and limits public scrutiny.“Section 8(1)(j), the deletion, is changing the whole concept of news,” Divan submitted according to news agency PTI.The petition further questions the Centre’s powers to requisition information under the DPDP Act, claiming they could affect news organisations’ ability to report on matters of public interest.The Supreme Court is scheduled to hear the matter on November 17 alongside pending cases.
Article Summary: Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) challenges provisions of the Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and its accompanying rules. The association had alleged that the act infringe press freedom and the right to information. The matter will be heard next on November 17 along with pending petitions.

Article Title: 'Breaking Bad' to 'Prison Break': Stalin takes fresh swipe at Vijay govt after 17 inmates flee jail
Article Text:
Stalin doubles down on TV series jibes at Vijay govt after Theni jailbreak

How 17 inmates allegedly escaped

NEW DELHI: Former Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin on Tuesday launched a fresh cinematic salvo at the ruling TVK government, following up his 'Breaking Bad' jibe with a 'Prison Break' reference to target chief minister C Joseph Vijay over the escape of 17 inmates from a Theni sub-jail.The DMK supremo's remarks came after 17 undertrial inmates allegedly escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district late on Monday night.Former CM hit out at the TVK government, accusing the administration of failing to maintain law and order.Taking a swipe at the government led by actor-turned-politician Vijay, Stalin drew a parallel with the television series Prison Break, saying the state appeared to be witnessing a similar situation after two prisoners had earlier escaped from Puzhal prison.“Following Breaking Bad, Prison Break has now begun in Tamil Nadu too!” Stalin said in a post on X, questioning how such a large number of inmates could escape despite improved security arrangements and surveillance systems.He said the escape of 17 inmates was particularly alarming, mentioning that it was reportedly the first such incident since 1995. Stalin said the incident came soon after the escape of two prisoners from Puzhal prison, raising questions over prison security.Accusing the government of incompetence, the former chief minister said authorities had failed to keep track of criminals released on bail and were now struggling to prevent escapes from inside jails.“Criminals outside are committing crimes freely. Prisoners inside are also escaping without fear,” he said.Stalin further alleged that the TVK government was incapable of protecting the people of Tamil Nadu, describing it as a “completely useless, good-for-nothing administration”.He said the state had reached a point where people were being left to fend for themselves, and demanded accountability over the security lapses.This is not the first time Stalin has used a cinematic reference to target Vijay's government. Days earlier, he invoked 'Breaking Bad' following a multi-crore methamphetamine seizure in the state.The political attack followed the arrest of Boopalan, a TVK Nagapattinam district functionary and the party's Kilvelur election in-charge, by the Directorate of Revenue Intelligence (DRI). He was arrested for allegedly harbouring 135kg of methamphetamine, reportedly worth several crores of rupees.According to preliminary investigations, the 17 undertrial inmates allegedly feigned epileptic seizures to lure prison staff into opening their cell before attacking the guards and fleeing the premises.The incident took place at Thekkampatti sub-jail in Theni district late on Monday night. Four of the escapees have been rearrested, while 13 remain at large.Three prison personnel were injured in the incident. Grade II Police Constable Thangapandi suffered serious head injuries and was rushed to the Government Hospital at G Vilakku. Two other personnel sustained minor injuries.Praveen Kumar was the first of the four escapees to be caught. The other three, identified as Silambarasan of Theni and Raja Sikandar and Rajkumar of Madurai, were re-arrested during search operations on Tuesday.
Article Summary: Former Tamil Nadu CM MK Stalin launches fresh cinematic salvo at the ruling TVK government. He follows up his 'Breaking Bad' jibe with a 'Prison Break' reference to target chief minister C Joseph Vijay. 17 undertrial inmates allegedly escaped from Thekkampatti sub-jail in Tamil Nadu's Theni district late on Monday night.

Article Title: 10 things we learnt about Gen Z beauty from Myntra's newest report
Article Text:
Beauty in the Age of Gen Z

. Gen Z's beauty story is not just a metro story

They give beauty a bigger share of their wallet

3. Prevention is the new correction

They read the ingredient list before they buy

Minis are the gateway to luxury

K-Beauty is still commanding the Gen Z beauty buyer’s attention

7. Men’s skincare is no longer a niche

8. Video and creators drive discovery

9.

Gen Z is loyal and backs Indian brands.

10. The wishlist shows what's next, and the market has room to grow

Sharon Pais, Head of Myntra, said:

The bigger picture on Myntra

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Myntra by Times Internet's Spotlight team.

For Gen Z, beauty is no longer about covering up imperfections. It is about preventing them. This generation is building everyday routines around skincare, reaching for sunscreen all year round and checking ingredient lists before they buy. That shift is changing what young shoppers expect from beauty products and the brands that sell them., a new report released by Myntra, looks at how these more preventive, ingredient-conscious consumers are reshaping India's beauty market. Here's what stood out.Half of Gen Z's beauty buyers on Myntra live in Tier 2 and 3 cities, and these cities account for half of the platform's international beauty demand. Ludhiana, Patna, Bhopal, Indore, Guwahati, Surat, Varanasi and Imphal are among those driving growth. Their baskets include serums, toners, sunscreens and hair masks alongside everyday staples.2.Gen Z gives beauty and personal care a 75% higher share of wallet, and spend per customer is up 1.2X year on year, alongside a fast-growing customer base.Sun protection is now a year-round habit. SPF purchases among Gen Z shoppers are up 60% YoY. Searches are up 80% for spray sunscreens, 70% for ingredient-led sunscreens and 60% for tinted ones.4.Gen Z is seeking out ingredients such as Centella asiatica, copper peptides, azelaic acid and panthenol, and prefers gel-based, fragrance-free, non-sticky texturesEfficacy and ingredients count as much as the brand name.5.53% of luxe makeup orders on Myntra now include a mini, and minis make up 14% of luxe units sold, led by lipstick, perfume and face primer. M.A.C, Kayali, Smashbox and Salvatore Ferragamo get more than half of their new customers through minis.6.K-Beauty demand is up 200% YoY, with searches up more than 300%. Myntra now offers 1,000+ SKUs from 90+ K-Beauty brands, 30+ of them added in the last year.Men’s skincare orders on Myntra grew 78% YoY, and Gen Z is leading the charge. Skincare is increasingly something young men shop for as seriously as anyone else, and it is one of the fastest-moving parts of the category.Myntra has ~82,000 active beauty creators, and UGC beauty content is up 40% YoY. Nearly 2 in 3 new beauty creator registrations over the last four months are Gen Z.Repeat Gen Z orders are up ~70% this year. D2C beauty has grown consistently this year, with Gen Z shoppers being 25% more likely to try a homegrown, D2C brand Plum, Minimalist, Foxtale, The Derma Co. and Chemist at Play are among those driving growth.Gen Z's wishlist already points to lactic acid, tranexamic acid and foundation-SPF hybrids. The wider market is expected to grow from ~$23bn to ~$40bn*, yet India spends only ~$15 per head on beauty, against $38 in China and $383 in the US*."Beauty and personal care is one of Myntra's strongest growth engines. For Gen Z, beauty is self-expression. It's how they show up, plan their looks and live their social lives. They try premium and international brands through minis, find new ones through creators and K-Beauty, and choose on ingredients and efficacy, in cities across the country. The brands that win will meet this shopper early, make discovery easy and earn trust through the product and its ingredients. "Beauty is roughly 1 in 5 units ordered on Myntra. Myntra offers over 2 lakh styles from 4,500+ brands, including 360+ international brands. Tech is helping shoppers choose with confidence: Virtual Try-On makes shoppers 2X more likely to buy, and Skin Analyzer lifts conversion by ~58%. For those who want it fast, Beauty on M-Now spans ~600 brands, with delivery in little as 30 minutes.The report was unveiled at the Myntra Beauty IRL event in Mumbai, alongside a panel discussion on The New Indian Beauty Consumer. It is based on Myntra platform data, buying behaviour and search trends from August 2025 to August 2026, covering Gen Z shoppers, and is read alongside trend-spotting by Myntra's creative and curation teams.*Market estimates are from Redseer.
Article Summary: Half of Gen Z's beauty buyers on Myntra live in Tier 2 and 3 cities. K-Beauty demand is up 200% YoY, with searches up more than 300%. Nearly 2 in 3 new beauty creator registrations over the last four months are Gen Z. Sun protection is now a year-round habit.

Article Title: Lawrence Bishnoi moved to high-security Ahemdabad jail block
Article Text:
Lawrence Bishnoi (File Photo)

Lawrence put in block which also houses 2008 blasts convicts

NEW DELHI: Gangster Lawrence Bishnoi is learnt to have been recently shifted to “Do sau kholi”, a specialised high-security block at Ahmedabad’s Sabarmati Central Jail housing 200 dangerous inmates accused of terrorism and other heinous offences, sources say. To ensure total isolation and prevent inter-cell movement, the block has four segregated sections of 50 prisoners each. The size of his cell is roughly 7.5x11 ft.The move is part of an elaborate security plan to clip the wings of Bishnoi.Prior to 2023-2024, Lawrence routinely made extortion calls, circulated threatening audio and video messages to manage his network and even gave interviews from different jails. But investigators have reported zero direct calls or communication originating from him over the past two years.Over the past two years, investigators have reported zero direct calls or communication originating from Lawrence Bishnoi.“Block 200” is a maximum-security area within Sabarmati jail which holds convicts of the 2008 serial blasts case and other serious cases and is generally the zone for prisoners convicted of serious offences and restrained from moving outside the prison under the provisions of Section 303 of the BNSS.Before this, Lawrence was held in “Dus Kholi,” a smaller high-security enclosure accommodating just 10 inmates. Prior to that, he was in Tihar jail and different jails in Punjab. Recorded calls of Lawrence threatening call centre owners and even a purported conversation with gangster Shehzad Bhatti had surfaced while he was in these jails.Deprived of physical interaction and digital access, Lawrence now lives under round-the-clock solitary surveillance. He reportedly maintains a disciplined, ascetic lifestyle inside his cell — spending mornings in meditation, regularly reciting the Hanuman Chalisa, observing fasts and maintaining a vegetarian diet. His only interactions with outside world involve attending court hearings via video conferencing and discussing his legal strategy with his lawyer.However, while he is isolated inside Sabarmati jail, his syndicate continues to operate globally through a decentralised chain of command. A ‘shadow cabinet’ comprising his top henchmen runs its day-to-day operations from foreign safe havens.Key members of the core group coordinate recruitment, tasking and logistics, besides sharing screenshots. There is a parallel group which deals with planning, financing and target selection. Most of them, including kingpins Goldy Brar and Rohit Godara, have gone underground since the FBI’s Operation Hardball.
Article Summary: Lawrence put in block which also houses 2008 blasts convicts. To ensure total isolation, the block has four segregated sections of 50 prisoners each. The size of his cell is roughly 7.5x11 ft. The move is part of an elaborate security plan to clip the wings of Bishnoi.

Article Title: On Accession Day, Mehbooba blasts Sheikh Abdullah, says his pro-Pak politics turned Kashmiris suspects
Article Text:
Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) President Mehbooba Mufti addresses the gathering during Accession Day, at party office, in Srinagar.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

SRINAGAR: PDP president Mehbooba Mufti Monday launched a scathing attack on National Conference founder Sheikh Mohammad Abdullah, accusing him of fuelling anti-India sentiment despite having championed Jammu & Kashmir’s accession to India and providing what she called “Hindutva forces” an opportunity to target the region’s special status.Addressing a party convention at the PDP headquarters here on the occasion of Accession Day (Oct 26), Mehbooba said the people of J&K had willingly joined India and that the country’s initial leadership had maintained good relations with the region and its people.“The first prime minister of the country, Jawaharlal Nehru, had said J&K would be a show window for the world. I do not know what happened between Sheikh Abdullah and the central leadership that Sheikh Abdullah, who was flagbearer of accession, turned against it and began saying we now wanted Pakistan, a plebiscite and separatism,” the former CM said.She said Sheikh Abdullah’s politics strengthened “Hindutva forces” across the country, giving them an excuse to target J&K’s special status and intensify their campaign for “one nation, one flag and one Constitution.”“Sheikh Abdullah was the real flag-bearer of bringing Jammu & Kashmir, a Muslim-majority region, into India. But he became unhappy and launched the plebiscite movement. From 1953, he spent 22 years pursuing that politics.As a result of it, the people of Jammu & Kashmir came to be viewed with suspicion by the country,” she said.“Look at J&K today. It is one of the most militarised regions in the world. There are seven to eight lakh troops including security personnel, paramilitary forces deployed here,” Mehbooba said.She said Sheikh Abdullah returned to the political mainstream in 1975 after reaching an accord with the Centre and abandoned the slogans he had raised for 22 years, including those relating to a plebiscite and Pakistan. However, she said, the people of J&K continued to pay the price for his politics of 22 years.“Even after 80 years, J&K continues to suffer,” she said.Mehbooba said recently at the United Nations, the president of Turkey, who has nothing to do with J&K, raised the issue. As usual, Pakistan PM Shehbaz Sharif also raised it. “In response, our govt said J&K is an integral part of India,” she said.Mehbooba said J&K will be discussed in Punjab and Uttar Pradesh elections, but no one talks about the people of J&K. “Instead, they talk to us through agencies like the NIA and CBI, through the UAPA and the Public Safety Act (PSA),” she said.“India is a great country with a rich culture and heritage, its people are great. But the people of J&K continue to be treated as they were in 1947,” she said. “In 2019, they pushed Jammu & Kashmir into further decline by taking away our rights and abrogating Article 370,” she said.The 79th Accession Day is being celebrated across J&K on Monday. On Oct 26, 1947, Maharaja Hari Singh, the then ruler of the princely state, signed the Instrument of Accession, formally agreeing to Jammu & Kashmir’s accession to India, which came into effect on Oct 27, 1947.

NEW DELHI: High fever and laboured breathing threatened the life of Oho-Tahane, a child from Jarawa tribe of Andaman and Nicobar Islands. With specialist care out of reach, health workers turned to e-Sanjeevani for remote consultation. The doctor diagnosed pneumonia, and timely expert intervention helped the child’s condition improve rapidly.Oho-Tahane, a member of one of India’s most vulnerable tribal groups, is among over 50 crore cases, many in far flung areas, facilitated by the national telemedicine service since its launch in Nov 2019.The service’s achievement was highlighted by PM Narendra Modi in his ‘Mann Ki Baat’ address Sunday, as he also cited how e-Sanjeevani enabled a doctor to guide a medical team in treating Kunhi Koya (60) in Kalpeni, Lakshadweep, and helped ensure medical assistance for pregnant Kunjang Dolma in Himalayan region of Zanskar.Developed by C-DAC Mohali under the health ministry, e-Sanjeevani facilitates 2.5-3 lakh daily consultations, offers services in 15 languages and is available across all 36 states and UTs. Women account for 57.1% of the platform’s utilisation, while people aged 46 and above account for 40.1% of consultations. Those aged 60 and above account for 16.2%. The platform has recorded a peak of 6,30,315 consultations in a single day.Modi credited the platform’s reach to dedication of doctors, public trust and the effective use of technology. He highlighted 1.9 lakh Ayushman Arogya Mandirs, saying they were bringing healthcare closer to rural communities and evolving into wellness centres for village panchayats. Regular health check-ups were becoming more common in rural areas, he said, with e-Sanjeevani playing an important role.The PM also highlighted advances in brain research, referring to Sudha Gopalakrishnan Brain Centre at IIT-Madras, which he inaugurated this month. The centre has developed a brain imaging technology platform to create high resolution digital 3D images of human brain. Its mission is to map and study 100 human brains in detail using Param Shakti supercomputer..Modi said the initiative could deepen understanding of the brain, particularly as conditions such as Alzheimer’s disease and dementia lack a definitive cure. Data from the 100 brains will be available as an open-source resource for researchers, the PM added.

Article Title: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to government than needed, says Justice Kaul

NEW DELHI: Former CJI D Y Chandrachud was more deferential to the govt than necessary in matters of judicial appointments, former SC judge Justice Sanjay Kishan Kaul has said in his forthcoming book ‘Without Fear Or Favour’, and claimed that he was prevented from hearing petitions for re-examination of the validity of provisions of PMLA.Kaul also claimed Justice Chandrachud had, allegedly under pressure from govt, withdrawn a case from him in which a bench headed by him had questioned delays in implementation of the SC collegium’s resolutions for appointment of judges. This, he said, “troubled him the most” as the case was assigned years ago and was taken away all of a sudden.Reacting to the claims, Justice Chandrachud said, “There was never even a dissent by any member of the collegium over any name during discussions for appointments to the SC.”Sources said resolutions passed by the collegium for appointments to the SC during Justice Chandrachud’s tenure were unanimous and signed by all members of the collegium without recording a single dissent.In this case, a bench of Justices Kaul and Sudhanshu Dhulia had pulled up govt for its alleged pick-and-choose policy in clearing names sent by the collegium and had on Nov 20, 2023, asked why Centre was not transferring four judges from Gujarat HC and not appointing two Sikh lawyers for Punjab and Haryana HC as recommended by the collegium.The case was thereafter taken away from his bench and it has not been listed in the last three years.In an interview to Karan Thapar for The Wire, Justice Kaul claimed the former CJI took him aside during a collegium meeting and asked whether he should telephone govt to ascertain its views on the proposed appointments. Justice Kaul said pre-approval from govt before discussions in the collegium was a matter of concern.“This has unfortunately become a practice of names being discussed, and some kind of previous discussion with govt. That used to happen. It has been happening, I think before CJI Chandrachud and after. That is why it troubles me,” he said, adding that there was nothing wrong in holding consultations with govt, but it should happen only after the collegium’s decision and not before.Asked whether Justice Chandrachud was too deferential to govt, Justice Kaul said, “There is a judicial side and there is an administrative side of the Chief Justice of India. I wouldn’t be concerned with the judicial side. I believe he had both the intellectual heft and the capacity and hard work to do so. But in consultations with govt and collaboration, I felt he was more deferential than necessary to carry it forward.Justice Kaul said he tried to discourage Justice Chandrachud from discussing everything with govt beforehand as it could create its own problems. Asked whether Justice Chandrachud failed to live up to the high expectations from him, Justice Kaul said, “I would say that expectations were higher from him.”TOI has reported how Justice Kaul had vigorously and successfully pushed many names for judgeship as part of the SC and HC collegiums and three of his proposals had met with resistance from other members of the panel. The then CJI had tactically refrained from holding collegium meetings to avoid embarrassing situations.In reply to the TOI article, Justice Kaul had sent a rejoinder and said, “There was no question of insistence of appointment of those suggested by me and all recommendations have been made by consensus. That other collegium members had reservations and I pushed the names, thus, seem to be a flight of your imagination.”

Article Title: A cooling-off period for MPs, MLAs who quit? SC to decide

NEW DELHI: In a development that could impact politics of shifting loyalties, SC Monday agreed to examine whether an MLA or an MP who contests a by-election caused by their voluntary resignation should be made to bear the entire expenses incurred by Election Commission in conducting the previous poll.Senior advocate Shoeb Alam told a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana that six persons elected on AIADMK tickets to the Tamil Nadu assembly had resigned in May and June after declaration of results and defected to TVK. Two of them resigned, causing by-elections which they went on to win, this time as TVK candidates.Appearing for petitioner K Suthan, Alam said the court was required to examine whether a person who voluntarily resigned as an MLA or MP should be barred for five years from contesting a state or parliamentary election. SC issued notices to Centre, EC and the six AIADMK MLAs who resigned and defected.The trend of lawmakers crossing over to the party in office and quitting their seats to avoid disqualification has caught on. The petitioner has sought legislative or regulatory measures “to create a mechanism for ensuring financial accountability of elected representatives who prematurely resign from their seats without legally recognised compelling circumstances, including introduction of an ‘Election Expenditure Security’ to recover cost of resultant bye-elections”.He has requested the court to direct Centre and EC to examine and initiate “necessary legislative and/or regulatory measures to introduce a statutory disqualification or a reasonable cooling-off period to prevent elected representatives who voluntarily and prematurely resign from contesting subsequent polls”. Suthan has suggested a five-year cooling-off period.The petitioner contended that none of the vacancies in the six seats was caused by death, permanent disability, disqualification or other compelling circumstance warranting a bypoll. “Public shouldn’t be made to pay twice for polls to the same constituency because of an individual’s personal or political choice to resign,” he said.Refusing to entertain Suthan’s petition, a Madras HC bench led by CJ S A Dharmadhikari had said, “We are being asked to design a punitive and financial regime that would operate as a fresh disqualification under Constitution and would curtail statutory right to contest election.In our opinion, the same is a matter of legislative policy, not of judicial direction.”“Right to resign a legislative seat is itself a facet of the constitutional scheme governing membership of a House and cannot be burdened with extra-statutory conditions by judicial order, however sound the underlying concern may be,” the HC had said while refusing the plea to impose a five-year cooling-off period on MPs and MLAs who voluntarily resign from their seats in the House concerned.

NEW DELHI: Challenging the constitutional validity of various provisions of Digital Personal Data Protection (DPDP) Act and subsequent rules framed by govt, Digital News Publishers Association (DNPA) is likely to move Supreme Court, alleging that they were violative of the fundamental right to freedom of speech and expression and threatened the full spectrum of journalistic activity.“It is prayed that sections 7, 17(2), 18, 19, 27, 29, 36, 37, 44(3) of DPDP Act and Rules 16, 17, and 23 of DPDP Rules framed under Section 40 be declared void to the extent they are in contravention of fundamental rights of the Constitution,” said the petition of the association, representing 21 of India’s leading media organisations.“The sections mentioned above fail to provide any exemption in favour of journalistic activity as a distinct class of processing, entitled to constitutional protection under Article 14 and 19(l)(a) of the Constitution and threaten the full spectrum of journalistic activity carried out by journalists, ground reporters, citizens, whistleblowers, RTI activists, and other stakeholders, and strikes at the core of our democratic framework and runs contrary to the basic tenets of the Constitution. ”It said publishers, editors, reporters and correspondents will be brought within a regime of notice and prior consent, compelled erasure and verifiable consent, obligations that cannot be reconciled with the ordinary functioning of the press. Questioning the validity of Section 44(3) of the Act, which places every category of “personal information” beyond the reach of disclosure, without regard to whether it relates to a public activity, the petition said it dismantled the balancing mechanism between right to privacy and right to information that operated for two decades.“These provisions, taken collectively, constitute a disproportionate and excessive curtailment of the fundamental right to free speech and expression and the implicit right to know and access information as recognised under Article 19(l)(a). DPDP Act creates restrictions on the fundamental right to free speech and expression in relation to the dissemination of news,” the petition added.
Article Summary: Digital News Publishers Association is set to move the Supreme Court challenging provisions of the DPDP Act and Rules. Article Title: SC restores Karnataka land, says government can acquire only for public purpose
Article Text:
Supreme Court quashes Karnataka's 1988 acquisition of 59 acres near Bengaluru for a housing society, restores land to owners and orders Rs 50,000 compensation to litigants.

NEW DELHI: Holding that govt can acquire land from citizens only for public purpose and not for the benefit of some person or organisation, Supreme Court Monday quashed a 1988 acquisition of about 59 acres of land near Bengaluru by Karnataka govt for a cooperative housing society and restored the land to its owners after 38 years.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating “the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens”. It said that illegal acquisitions were made through fraud and undue influence and directed the state govt to pay Rs 50,000 to all litigant landowners who had challenged the process.“Condemnation of privately owned land for public purpose can only be with authority of law and with just compensation being paid. That such authority of law can be exercised only for public purpose is without cavil, with just compensation being an ancillary right, which does not by itself justify an acquisition. However just the compensation be, if the authority of law is lacking or the public purpose is absent, there can be no eminent domain exercised,” the court said.SC upheld the single-bench HC order,which said that it was at the instigation of middlemen that the state employed its machinery to acquire land for the society.
Article Summary: Supreme Court quashes Karnataka's 1988 acquisition of 59 acres near Bengaluru for a housing society. Justices J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran held that the whole process of land acquisition is indicating ‘the fraud played on unsuspecting citizens’

New Delhi: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, the Supreme Court verbally assured electors on Monday. It allayed fears that use of Form 6, which asks applicants to declare they are fresh voters, for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration.The statement came from a bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohan while hearing a PIL against large-scale exclusion of names from Maharashtra ’s draft electoral roll and as a response to senior advocate Aravind Datar’s plea that using Form 6 for re-inclusion would amount to lying under oath.The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, to be published on Nov 6, it could grant them more time to submit their documents for the purpose. A similar concern was raised by advocate Prashant Bhushan 10 days earlier while questioning the EC’s directive that voters whose names were deleted from Delhi’s draft electoral roll during SIR exercise use Form 6 to restore them in draft rolls.Datar said that with two crore voters excluded from Maharashtra’s draft electoral roll, including 1.22 crore on grounds of logical discrepancy, and the deadline for claims and objections ending on Oct 26, many voters who were removed on flimsy and non-existent grounds would have little chance of getting names restored.The senior advocate requested the bench to extend the Oct-26 deadline for those seeking inclusion of their names in the electoral roll. The bench asked the EC to file its response to the PIL by Nov 5 and said it would examine on that day whether extra time would be required for those seeking inclusion of names.Datar said, “In Maharashtra, 33% of voters have been deleted. In Mumbai, 40% of the voters have been excluded. What is happening is people are asked to fill Form 6, which is meant for fresh voters. There is no provision for a person who had voted in the last three or four elections to get his name restored in the voter list. If he fills Form 6, which is meant for registration of fresh voters, then he would face prosecution for false declaration. ”However, the CJI allayed these fears and said, “No one will be prosecuted for filling Form 6 seeking re-entering of their names in voter lists.” Datar said that since there was no imminent election in Maharashtra, the SC could direct EC not to finalise the electoral roll for the state on Nov 6 and postpone the schedule to enable genuine voters to re-enter them in voter lists. The bench also said, “If we find, even after the publication of the final electoral roll, that there are people who are genuine voters but still excluded, we can extend time for them to submit documents for the purpose of re-entering their names in voter lists. ”
Article Summary: No one will be prosecuted for using Form 6 to re-enter their name in electoral rolls, Supreme Court assures electors. It allayed fears that use of Form 6 for re-inclusion in draft electoral rolls could invite prosecution for false declaration. The bench also said that if it found there were genuine voters whose names could not be included in the final electoral list, it could grant them more time to submit their documents.

NEW DELHI: Paving the way for roll out of flex fuel vehicles (FFVs) that can run on up to E100 — nearly 100% pure ethanol or about 93-95% ethanol-blended with petrol — road transport ministry Monday modified changes in Central Motor Vehicles Rules.This comes barely months before some car manufacturers launch their E100 models.FFVs with an internal combustion engine can run on petrol, biofuels like ethanol or methanol, or any mixture of both stored in a single fuel tank. E100 fuels are “intended only for vehicles designed and certified to use it”.Officials said this is not applicable for other vehicles.“Vehicles that use E20 or normal fuel can’t use E85 or E100 fuel. Hence, the notification doesn’t require owners of existing vehicles to switch to these fuel categories or modify their vehicles now or in the future,” said a transport ministry official.TOI has learnt that the change in rules was essential for type approval and registration of FFVs on E100 considering that vehicle manufacturers are ready with their products.Depending on the vehicle’s design and certification, the range of blending may extend to E85 or E100, a fuel predominantly consisting of ethanol.Flex fuel technology is used in countries such as Brazil and the US.Ethanol has a lower fossil carbon footprint than conventional petrol and the use of higher ethanol blends can help reduce tailpipe emission of carbon monoxide (CO) and certain hydrocarbons. Greater ethanol use will also reduce dependence on import of crude oil.While govt notification will enable OEMs to manufacture FFVs, this won’t be enough to push adoption of these vehicles, experts said. This is evident as even after almost seven months of the launch of E85 cars, only 17 such vehicles have been registered.Industry players called reduction in GST on FFVs from 28% to 5% (on par with EVs) to bring down vehicle cost for buyers and compensate for mileage loss, which is about 27% while using E100 fuel.Besides, they sought a reduction in fuel cost to around Rs 75 a litre.But a bigger problem is availability of E100 given that there are only a handful of pumps, although it can run on other grades of ethanol-blended fuel.
Article Summary: Road transport ministry Monday modified changes in Central Motor Vehicles Rules. FFVs with an internal combustion engine can run on petrol, biofuels like ethanol or methanol. E100 fuels are “intended only for vehicles designed and certified to use it’

10 lakh people, up to 20,000 vehicles

21 markets at risk

'We hear you': Rahul Gandhi

The Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to postpone the party’s proposed November 1 rally at Delhi’s Ramlila Maidan, warning that it could disrupt business across 21 major wholesale and retail markets during the peak festive shopping season and cause losses of up to Rs 10,000 crore.The traders’ body has asked Congress to defer the rally until November 10, after Bhai Dooj, or shift it to an alternative venue away from commercial areas. The Congress has claimed that the rally could draw 10 lakh people.In a letter to Rahul Gandhi, a copy of which was also sent to Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, CTI chairman Brijesh Goyal raised concerns about possible barricading and road closures on October 31 and November 1. He said traders were worried about whether customers would be able to reach shops during the crucial festive period, news agency PTI reported.According to the CTI, a gathering of 10 lakh people could bring between 15,000 and 20,000 vehicles into Delhi. These could include 10,000 to 12,000 buses and 5,000 to 7,000 smaller vehicles, such as cars, minibuses and tempo travellers.The organisation questioned where these vehicles would be parked, claiming there was no authorised parking facility for even 200 vehicles in the immediate vicinity of Ramlila Maidan.It also warned that congestion could spill into the narrow lanes of Old Delhi, many of which are only 10 to 12 feet wide. A single truck getting stuck in these lanes could trigger traffic jams lasting several hours, it said.The CTI identified 21 markets that could be affected by the rally, including Chandni Chowk, Sadar Bazaar, Khari Baoli, Bhagirath Palace, Chawri Bazaar, Kashmere Gate, Karol Bagh, Daryaganj, Paharganj, Jama Masjid and Lajpat Rai Market.The body cited the October 10 event at Jantar Mantar, claiming that a gathering of around 3,000 to 4,000 people had disrupted movement across central Delhi and caused traders losses of Rs 3,000 crore.It projected that the November 1 rally could bring commercial activity across Old Delhi to a standstill, with losses potentially reaching Rs 10,000 crore.The CTI has proposed Burari Ground or Jawaharlal Nehru Stadium as alternative venues if the rally cannot be postponed. It has urged the Congress leadership to consider the concerns of traders and minimise disruption to business during the festive season.Congress leader Rahul Gandhi expressed solidarity with Delhi’s traders, alleging that government restrictions had disrupted business by shutting metro services, sealing roads and locking down the capital.Linking the disruption to his allegations of “vote chori”, Rahul demanded that Prime Minister Narendra Modi sack Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, whom he referred to as “Accused No. 4”.“To every trader in Delhi: We love you and hear you. The Govt shut the metro, sealed our roads and locked down our capital. With a stolen vote nothing is safe - your shop, your savings, your children’s future. Tell Modi to sack accused no. 4, Gyanesh Kumar and the protests will stop in 30 seconds,” Rahul said.Delhi traders sought Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s intervention over losses allegedly caused by the October 10 protest called by the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), demanding compensation from those responsible for the disruption.The Automotive Parts Merchants Association (Regd.), Delhi, said customers stayed away from markets for four to five days before and after the protest call, resulting in heavy business losses.The association had said October, November and December were crucial for traders because of the festive season, including Navratri, Dhanteras and Diwali. It warned that repeated disruptions during this period could threaten the livelihoods of shopkeepers and their employees.The trade body called for a transparent assessment of the losses and sought full compensation from the principal organisers and participants responsible for the disruption, arguing that traders should not bear the financial burden.It said shop earnings were used to support traders’ families and employees, pay rent, fund children’s education and cover medical expenses for elderly parents.The association also flagged the absence of basic emergency arrangements, including ambulances, fire services and first aid, at protests, warning that such gaps could lead to serious accidents.
Article Summary: Chamber of Trade and Industry (CTI) has urged Congress leader Rahul Gandhi to postpone the party’s proposed November 1 rally. It warns that it could disrupt business across 21 major wholesale and retail markets and cause losses of up to Rs 10,000 crore. The traders’ body has asked Congress to defer the rally until November 10, after Bhai Dooj.

Article Title: Centre to train 10,000 healthcare workers in drug de-addiction by 2029

NEW DELHI: With the Centre targeting a drug-free India by 2029, the health ministry has launched a nationwide capacity-building programme to train 10,000 healthcare professionals in the prevention, diagnosis and treatment of substance use disorders, including addiction to alcohol, opioids and other drugs.Union health minister J P Nadda launched the programme on Monday under the Vision Document on Narcotic Control 2026-2029, stressing that tackling substance abuse requires coordinated action by healthcare, social welfare and law enforcement agencies. The ministry aims to train 2,000 personnel in the current financial year, followed by 3,000 in 2027-28 and 5,000 in 2028-29.The programme will be implemented through six central government institutions under the Drug De-addiction Programme, with the National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS, serving as the coordinating centre. The other institutions are NIMHANS, Bengaluru; PGIMER, Chandigarh; Central Institute of Psychiatry, Ranchi; Dr Ram Manohar Lohia Hospital, Delhi; and AIIMS Bhubaneswar.The training will combine live online sessions, self-paced courses and in-person programmes. Doctors and medical officers will undergo a 12-week online training course featuring lectures and clinical case discussions, while nurses, community health officers, auxiliary nurse midwives, counsellors and psychologists will have access to specialised modules.The curriculum will cover substances ranging from alcohol and cannabis to opioids, sleeping tablets and inhalants, as well as addiction among vulnerable groups, including women and adolescents.More than 800 nominations have already been received through the health ministry and the National Health Mission for online and offline training. Around 150 personnel from de-addiction centres supported by the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment are also expected to undergo in-person training over the next two months.Nadda said fragmented efforts among government departments had created gaps in coordination and service delivery. Effective implementation of the narcotic control strategy, he said, would require clearly defined responsibilities, sustained inter-ministerial coordination and collective accountability. He also stressed the need to strengthen de-addiction centres through training, institutional support and adequate resources.At the launch, Nadda released the second edition of. First published in 2005, the revised manual incorporates advances in the understanding and treatment of addiction and is intended to help doctors manage substance use disorders in both specialised facilities and general healthcare settings.The initiative follows the Vision Document on Narcotic Control unveiled by Union home minister Amit Shah in June 2026. Besides enforcement against drug trafficking, the strategy assigns the health ministry the task of expanding access to evidence-based addiction treatment by strengthening the skills of medical and allied healthcare personnel.Officials said the programme would draw on the clinical expertise and training infrastructure of the six institutions to improve the availability and quality of addiction care across states and Union territories.
Article Summary: The programme will be implemented through six central government institutions. The training will combine live online sessions, self-paced courses and in-person programmes. Article Title: 'Veto should be held by all permanent members': India at UN
Article Text:
Parvathaneni Harish called for comprehensive Security Council reforms, arguing that all permanent members of an expanded Council must have equal rights and responsibilities

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: India has called for comprehensive reforms of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC), saying all permanent members of a reformed Council must have the same rights and responsibilities, including the power of veto.Delivering India's statement at the United Nations, India's permanent representative Parvathaneni Harish said the veto should be exercised with restraint and must not become a tool for narrow political interests, particularly on matters concerning international peace and security.India also opposed proposals to create a separate category of permanent members without the veto or with fewer powers, arguing that such an arrangement would deepen existing inequalities within the Council."India's position on the veto is principled and well known. It is aligned with the Common African Position. We reiterate that as long as the veto exists, it must be held by all permanent members of a reformed Council. Fairness and justice demand that all permanent members enjoy the same rights and responsibilities," news agency ANI quoted Harish as saying."A new category of permanent members, with or without the veto, would only further complicate a discussion that is already difficult, and would further entrench the very inequity we are seeking to correct.Periodic elections and the concept of permanency are fundamentally contradictory," Harish added.Harish said the veto had been used 331 times on around 200 resolutions during the UN's history. He noted that most vetoes, or threats to use them, had come from three of the five permanent members -- China, France, Russia, the United Kingdom and the United States."The record of the Veto is stark. Over the life of this Organisation, the veto has been exercised 331 times on around 200 resolutions. We also note that two out of the five permanent members have not exercised a veto for over three and a half decades, and most of the vetos or threats of vetos have emanated from only three of the P5," he said.He also questioned the effectiveness of accountability measures introduced in 2022, under which the UN General Assembly holds a debate whenever a permanent member exercises its veto. The continued use of the veto since the mechanism was adopted showed that it had not brought the expected change, he said.He also highlighted what he described as an “effective or de facto veto” in the Council's working methods. Under the practice of consensus, a single member can block presidential statements, press statements and decisions of sanctions committees, sometimes without providing an explanation, he said."The veto is not only what is cast in the open. There is also the 'effective or de facto veto' that every Council member, elected and non-elected, holds over presidential statements, press statements and the decisions of sanctions committees, where the unwritten rule of consensus allows a single member to hold or block a proposal, most often without explanation," Harish said.
Article Summary: India has called for comprehensive reforms of the United Nations Security Council (UNSC) India's permanent representative Parvathaneni Harish said all permanent members of a reformed Council must have the same rights and responsibilities, including the power of veto. India opposed proposals to create a separate category of permanent members without the veto.

Article Title: June 2025 decision to hold SIR taken unanimously, EC tells SC
Article Text:
EC tells SC that the June 24, 2025 decision to conduct nationwide SIR was unanimous, denying opposition claims that CEC Gyanesh Kumar acted unilaterally.

No substance in claim that Form 6 was amended by SIR orders: EC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission Monday filed an affidavit in SC that the chief election commissioner and the two election commissioners had unanimously taken the decision on June 24, 2025 to conduct nationwide SIR of electoral rolls and that there was no difference of opinion.The affidavit by deputy EC Bhanu Prakash Yeturu came with an unusual declaration that it was being filed with the approval of the CEC and the two ECs. “At the very outset, I state that the present affidavit has been approved for filing before the SC by a unanimous decision of the three members of the Election Commission, that is the 2 election commissioners and the chief election commissioner,” the affidavit said.The assertion contradicts the charge that CEC Gyanesh Kumar, at Modi government’s instance, unilaterally decided to conduct SIR of electoral rolls — the mainstay of the opposition’s “vote chori” campaign.The affidavit was filed in response to petitions, including one filed by Rahul Gandhi and other opposition leaders, following a news report that the two ECs — S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi — had approached the cabinet secretary because of their differences with the CEC over SIR-related issues.“Allegations based on the communication between ECs and the cabinet secretary are misconceived,” the EC said, adding that the letters by Sandhu and Joshi pertained to administrative matters.An office order came to be issued on July 28 by an IAS officer of the rank of additional secretary who had been posted on deputation to the commission pertaining to internal work allocation. On July 29, the two election commissioners wrote separate letters to the cabinet secretary in relation to this order and the conduct of the officer. In view of the joint direction of July 30 by the two ECs, the order of July 28 was never implemented,” the commission said. Responding to the petitions by Rahul and other INDIA bloc netas, the EC said all the petitions were based on a news article alleging that the commission had not been functioning in accordance with the procedure mandated in law, and allegations were also made questioning the integrity of the commission.It also issued a strong denial of the allegation, another key plank of the opposition’s offensive, that Form 6, as provided under Registration of Electors Rules, 1960, was amended by the commission by the SIR orders of June 24 and Oct 27 last year and May 14 this year. “There is no substance in the contention that Form 6 has been amended by the commission vide the SIR orders.” EC said Form 6 could be amended only by the Centre and what was changed was the introduction of a declaration to “enable the person seeking registration as a voter to dispense with the need for filing documents during the claims and objections period”.The ‘declaration’ was a document provided by the SIR orders and was not a part of Form 6, which was the statutory form for inclusion in the electoral rolls, it said, adding there was no significant change in the earlier and present declaration. The declaration that the affidavit was approved by the two ECs is significant because of the charge that the CEC’s “unilateral” calls on SIR-related issues were violative of the law, which required the poll body to take decisions unanimously or, when not possible, by majority. The opposition has demanded removal and prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar for violating the law.Denying the charge, the affidavit said that while the CEC, the ECs and even other officers may have expressed different views during deliberations, the decisions were taken in accordance with law. “The views by ECs/CEC of the commission during the decision-making process on the subjects before them are considered for arriving at the decision. It is upon consideration of all the views placed before the commission that the decision is taken and the orders are issued in accordance with the process,” the EC said.Explaining the process of decision-making in which views of all divisions concerned with the subject are considered in detail, the EC said, “In any such decision-making process, any suggestion, observation or query by the CEC or ECs either to the ECs or CEC or to any officer of the commission does not constitute a decision of the commission under Section 18 of the CEC and ECs (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023. ”It said the statute prefers a decision by unanimity but also provides for decision-making by majority in the three-member EC. The commission said the CEC and ECs had taken a unanimous decision on June 29 that “in case any person to whom notice has been issued during the ongoing SIR, for being unmapped and/or logical discrepancies, BLOs will visit the homes of such persons for collection of documents and thereafter upload them in the ECINet, for decision by the ERO”.“Such person shall not be called for hearing to the ERO/AERO officer. Only in exceptional circumstances, as defined by the ERO/AERO, will the hearing be held, preferably online. Any adult member of the family can be authorised by the elector to attend the hearing on their behalf,” EC said. Referring to the allegation relating to deletion of 97 voters in Goa, the commission said it had directed that no eligible voter should be left out of the rolls and pursuant to this, the BLOs conducted a house-to-house visit and found that 88 of the 97 had already filled Form 6 for inclusion of their names. Of the remaining nine, six were out of the country and three were Portuguese passport holders.
Article Summary: EC tells SC that the June 24, 2025 decision to conduct nationwide SIR was unanimous. Denies opposition claims that CEC Gyanesh Kumar acted unilaterally. No substance in claim that Form 6 was amended by SIR orders: EC.

Article Title: SC to UP police: Educate officers on investigation
Article Text:
Supreme Court slams UP police for "slipshod investigation", orders Rs 6 lakh compensation for man held six years without evidence.

Appalled at the way UP cops carried out probe: SC

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: In a severe indictment of Uttar Pradesh police for carrying out a “slipshod investigation” that resulted in a man being in custody for six years when there was no evidence against him, Supreme Court Monday said the state cannot shirk its responsibility to protect citizens and directed it to pay a compensation of Rs 6 lakh to him.“This is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a person’s life and liberty,” SC noted at the outset of its verdict.On Sept 30, in a separate matter, the top court had slammed UP police for not naming the accused in a road accident case.It would be better if investigations in all criminal cases were handed over to CBI if the state police works with an agenda and does cover-up jobs, court had said, noting the accused had not been named despite the complainant catching him on the spot and handing him over to police.In the present case, a bench of J B Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran said there was no evidence to implicate the person in a kidnapping and murder case. It noted he was never named in the FIR and police made him an accused on the basis that he was seen in CCTV footage. SC said it was “appalled at the manner in which investigation was carried out”. “It is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial.Based on a slipshod investigation, a haphazard prosecution was carried out, which resulted, fortunately, in the acquittal of the accused. We cannot but deprecate the manner in which the probe was carried out and prosecution conducted,” SC said. “State police would do well to educate their officers in the process of investigation.”Making the state accountable for police’s misdeed, the court said six years have been erased from the man’s life on the strength of a concocted story built on mere surmises and conjectures, and the state has to pay compensation.“The state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty. The investigation and prosecuting agencies exist not merely to, and by whatever means, bring in a conviction. They should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured but also to the accused,” the SC bench said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court slams UP police for "slipshod investigation", orders Rs 6 lakh compensation for man held six years without evidence. SC said it was “appalled at the manner in which investigation was carried out” “It is unfortunate that despite no evidence against the petitioner, he was imprisoned for six years as an undertrial,” SC said.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Monday urged the Supreme Court to summon all relevant records related to the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, following the Election Commission's affidavit stating that all decisions were taken unanimously.Congress MP Imran Masood said the issue was about adherence to the rules and that the questions concerned the deletion of votes and Form 6."The Supreme Court should summon all the relevant records; even if all three agreed, the core issue remains 'Form 6'. The issue is the theft of votes," he added.This comes hours after the poll panel submitted a counter-affidavit in the Supreme Court, defending its functioning and the conduct of the SIR exercise.The poll body rejected allegations of irregularities and questioned the basis of a petition challenging its decision-making process.The Election Commission stated this in its response to pleas alleging that it took several decisions without the approval of the two election commissioners, including "changes" in Form 6.The law and the prescribed Form 6 for voter registration were not amended, the poll panel said in its counter-affidavit filed in the Supreme Court with the unanimous approval of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and the two election commissioners.The EC said the SIR orders issued on June 24, 2025, October 27, 2025, and May 14, 2026, were approved unanimously by the commission's three members - the Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) and two election commissioners.It said the CEC could not be restrained from functioning, as newspaper reports were not considered evidence in the eyes of the law.Earlier, on October 5, the top court said it would examine all decisions of the EC and annul those found not to be in accordance with the law, as it issued notices to the Centre and the poll body.The pleas were filed afterreported on September 25 that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had objected on record at least 14 times over the previous 10 months to decisions and orders on the SIR of electoral rolls that they said were issued without their knowledge or recommendation. NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Monday directed the Uttar Pradesh government to pay Rs 6 lakh in reparation to a man who spent six years in jail as an undertrial in a murder case before being acquitted. The apex court said that the years lost to a faulty investigation were a travesty of justice.Slamming the state police for a “slipshod investigation” and the prosecution for its haphazard handling of the case, a bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and K Vinod Chandran called the man a “victim of the system”. It said six years of his life had been erased based on a “concocted story” built on mere surmises and conjectures.The man had been in custody since November 14, 2019, in a murder case registered in Agra.The Supreme Court noted that the trial court acquitted him after finding that none of the four circumstances cited by the prosecution, including electronic evidence, had been proved.“This is a classic case of how an investigation should not be proceeded with, resulting in the prosecution putting into jeopardy a person's life and liberty,” the bench said.The court directed the state to pay the compensation within one month, acknowledging that the amount was small compared with the years he had spent behind bars.“We, hence, direct the state to pay an amount of Rs 6 lakh; though paltry in comparison to the years spent in custody, within a period of one month to the petitioner herein,” it said.The verdict came on a plea challenging an Allahabad High Court order in January that had denied the man bail. The Supreme Court had directed the trial court on March 23 to conclude the proceedings within three months. The trial was subsequently completed, and the accused was acquitted.The bench said the case highlighted the failure of investigating and prosecuting agencies to safeguard an individual's liberty despite the presumption of innocence.“The state cannot shirk from its responsibility to protect its citizens, especially when a person arraigned in a criminal case is presumed innocent until proven guilty,” it said.The court stressed that the role of investigating and prosecuting agencies was not simply to secure convictions, but to ensure justice for all parties, including the accused.“They should recognise themselves to be essential stakeholders in the justice delivery system, ensuring justice, not only to the victim, the de facto complainant and the injured, but also to the accused,” the bench said.The judges also expressed concern over the wider implications of such cases, saying they had encountered similar failures but that this one stood out for its severity.“We come across such travesty of justice in many matters, but in some, so blatant and shocking, as in this case, which requires reparation to the accused, who in turn is a victim of the system,” it said.The bench directed that a copy of its verdict be sent to the Uttar Pradesh director general of police and the state's home secretary. It also urged the police to train officers in proper investigative procedures, criticising the manner in which the case had been handled.The court said the acquittal was fortunate, given the consequences of the flawed investigation and prosecution for the man's life and liberty.
Article Summary: The man had been in custody since November 14, 2019, in a murder case registered in Agra. The verdict came on a plea challenging an Allahabad High Court order in January that had denied the man bail. The Supreme Court had directed the trial court on March 23 to conclude the proceedings within three months.
